# package capture

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canbus/capture"
```

Package capture reads and writes CAN traces and replays them.

Formats:

  - candump log (FormatCandump): the format of can-utils' candump -L and canplayer, one frame per line, "(1700000000.123456) can0 123#A1B2". Classical, CAN FD ("##" with the flags nibble), remote ("R"), error frames and the DLC 9..15 suffix ("\_F"). Timestamps have microseconds.
  - JSON Lines (FormatJSONL): the lossless format of this package, one JSON object per frame with every [canbus.Frame](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#Frame) field and nanosecond timestamps. Schema: schemas/capture-v1.schema.json.
  - pcap (FormatPCAP) and pcapng (FormatPCAPNG) with LINKTYPE\_CAN\_SOCKETCAN, as written by tcpdump and dumpcap and read by Wireshark: classical, CAN FD, remote, error and CAN XL frames. pcapng keeps interface names.
  - Vector ASC (FormatASC) and BLF (FormatBLF), the trace formats of CANoe/CANalyzer, read and written. Lossy: ASC and BLF carry no Linux error class (error frames are read as protocol errors). Their times are local wall-clock times without a zone: they are read and written in time.Local (set TZ to read a file from another zone).
  - PEAK TRC (FormatTRC), the trace format of PCAN-View and PCAN-Explorer: versions 1.0 to 2.1 read, 2.1 written (classical, CAN FD, remote and error frames). Times are local like ASC and BLF.

Readers and writers stream: a trace of any size is processed frame by frame. [Replay](#func-replay) sends a trace with its original, scaled or no timing.

## Variables

```go
var ErrUnknownFormat = errors.New("capture: unknown trace format")
```

ErrUnknownFormat reports input whose format could not be recognised.

```go
var ErrUnrepresentable = errors.New("capture: frame not representable in the format")
```

ErrUnrepresentable reports a frame a writer cannot store in its format without corrupting it: a timestamp outside the format's range (before 1970 or after 2106 in pcap, for example), or a channel number or name too large for its field. Nothing is written for that frame.

### func ParseFrame

```go
func ParseFrame(s string, f *canbus.Frame) error
```

ParseFrame parses the compact frame notation of cansend and candump:

	<id>#<data>            classical, data as hex pairs, '.' separators allowed
	<id>#<data>_<dlc>      classical with 8 bytes and a raw DLC of 9..F
	<id>#R[<len>]          remote frame, optional DLC 0..8
	<id>##<flags><data>    CAN FD, flags nibble: 1 = BRS, 2 = ESI, 4 = FDF (ignored)

\<id> has 3 hex digits for a standard and 8 for an extended identifier; an 8-digit identifier with bit 29 (0x20000000) set is an error frame. CAN FD data whose length is not a CAN FD length is padded with zeros to the next one, as the kernel transmits it.

### func RecordAll

```go
func RecordAll(ctx context.Context, sub *canbus.Subscription, w XLWriter, count int) (int, error)
```

RecordAll is [RecordFrames](#func-recordframes) for a subscription opened with [canbus.WithXL](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#WithXL) and a writer of CAN XL frames: it records CAN, CAN FD and CAN XL frames in the order the bus received them.

### func RecordFrames

```go
func RecordFrames(ctx context.Context, sub *canbus.Subscription, w Writer, count int) (int, error)
```

RecordFrames receives frames from sub and writes them to w until ctx ends, count frames were written (0: no limit) or the subscription ends. It returns the number of frames written. CAN XL frames are recorded with [RecordAll](#func-recordall).

### type ReplayOptions

```go
type ReplayOptions struct {
	// Speed scales the original timing: 1 replays with the recorded gaps,
	// 2 twice as fast, 0.5 at half speed. 0 sends as fast as possible.
	Speed float64
	// Filter selects the frames to send; nil sends all. Error frames are
	// never sent. CAN XL frames are selected as by [canbus.FilterSet.MatchXL].
	Filter *canbus.FilterSet
	// MaxFrames stops after this many frames were sent (0: no limit).
	MaxFrames int
	// MaxDuration stops when this much time has passed (0: no limit).
	MaxDuration time.Duration
	// Rate limits the transmission to this many frames per second (0: no
	// limit). It applies on top of Speed.
	Rate float64
	// Interfaces maps recorded interface names to the senders frames of
	// that interface go to. Frames of interfaces not in the map go to the
	// sender passed to Replay; nil sends everything there.
	Interfaces map[string]Sender
	// OnFrame, if set, is called after each frame was sent.
	OnFrame func(f *canbus.Frame)
	// OnXLFrame, if set, is called after each CAN XL frame was sent.
	OnXLFrame func(x *canbus.XLFrame)
}
```

ReplayOptions control [Replay](#func-replay). The zero value replays every frame as fast as possible.

### type ReplayStats

```go
type ReplayStats struct {
	Read     int // frames read from the trace
	Sent     int // frames sent
	Filtered int // frames not selected by the filter
	Skipped  int // error frames (which cannot be sent)
	// SkippedXL counts the CAN XL frames that were not sent because their
	// sender does not carry CAN XL (no [XLSender], or SendXL reports
	// [canbus.ErrUnsupported], as a socket opened without CAN XL does).
	SkippedXL int
	Elapsed   time.Duration // wall time of the replay
	Limited   bool          // MaxFrames or MaxDuration ended the replay
}
```

ReplayStats reports what [Replay](#func-replay) did.

#### func Replay

```go
func Replay(ctx context.Context, r Reader, s Sender, opts ReplayOptions) (st ReplayStats, err error)
```

Replay reads frames from r and sends them to s, streaming: memory use does not depend on the trace size. A reader of CAN XL frames ([XLReader](#type-xlreader)) has them replayed through senders that carry CAN XL ([XLSender](#type-xlsender)); see [ReplayStats.SkippedXL](#func-replaystats-skippedxl). It returns when the trace ends, a limit is reached, ctx ends or a send fails.
